source.title: Gibbs-Based Information Criteria and the Over-Parameterized Regime
source.authors: Haobo Chen; Greg Wornell; Yuheng Bu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures population risk and generalization across model size in a random-feature model, using Gibbs-based information criteria and MALA rather than the claim versions' standard-training setups.
record.gate_note: The paper's experiments test a random-feature model with a fixed random first layer and trained second-layer weights on synthetic linear-regression data. Cited results about deep networks and memorization are not this paper's results. Figure-only test-loss trends are recorded without reconstructing precise values.
record.test_reason: The study reports decreasing test MSE as a two-layer ReLU random-feature network widens beyond the authors' interpolation threshold, bearing on V2 in a new regression setting. Its fixed first layer, Gaussian-prior regularization and Gibbs sampling differ from V2's original training setup.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The proposed Gibbs-based BICs can select large random-feature models, but marginal likelihood does not reproduce population risk's double descent. Prior choice affects this mismatch; at fixed λ, KL penalties and generalization gaps show similar width-dependent trends, which the authors relate to the weighted squared-norm component.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic linear-regression data and a random-feature model with a fixed first layer; second-layer weights are sampled using MALA from a Gibbs distribution. The study focuses on information criteria and population risk, rather than the claim versions' natural-label classification setups and standard training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The mismatch between the BIC KL-divergence penalty and generalization error varies with prior parameter λ. The reported comparison also distinguishes under-parameterized and over-parameterized settings around p = n.

fits_no_version.finding: Gibbs-based BIC can favor larger models without reproducing population risk's double-descent curve.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Marginal-likelihood model selection need not track held-out risk in regularized random-feature regression.

fits_no_version.finding: The BIC KL penalty and generalization gap show similar width-dependent trends at fixed λ but disagree across prior settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agreement between a posterior-to-prior KL penalty and generalization gap depends on holding the prior setting fixed.

fits_no_version.finding: The weighted squared-norm component of BIC exhibits double descent and decreases beyond interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The weighted squared norm of posterior-mean weights can decline with width beyond interpolation in the tested random-feature model.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The main findings concern one synthetic random-feature regression setup, with a fixed random first layer and MALA sampling. Relevant experiment values are presented in figures without exact numerical values in the text; uncertainty for the reported main comparisons is not stated. The paper says it performs 50 runs per setting to ensure result accuracy and plot error bars, but the supplied main figures' underlying numeric results are not given.
record.rows_left_out: No additional independently stated outcomes beyond the figure-based findings and textual trend descriptions were identified. Cited prior work and plots whose trends are only mentioned as comparisons were not added as separate results.

untested.parts: Paired random-label memorization and natural-label generalization experiments.
Networks with both layers trained without explicit regularization; MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 classification; numerically verified zero training error at the width threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Different datasets and training methods justify a new-setting test of V2 rather than exclusion solely for departing from its original experiments. The interpolation peak itself is contextual evidence, not a separate V2 prediction. The appendix specifies ReLU activation, 600 MALA epochs and 50 runs per setting with error bars; the record's blanket statement that uncertainty was not reported needs qualification.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels are not tested.
No one-hidden-layer ReLU sweep on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10 is reported. The random-feature model's size sweep does not test this version's specified setup.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison is reported.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison is reported.
No large-batch training comparison is reported.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or competing generalization-measure comparison is reported.
No memorized-example removal experiment is reported.

rows.check: The qualitative result is explicitly stated: test loss peaks at p = n = 200 and then declines, eventually below under-parameterized levels. Missing exact plotted values does not prevent determining that direction. Distinguish data noise variance 0.1 from the fitted likelihood/posterior parameter σ = 0.05. Training includes explicit Gaussian-prior regularization; exact zero training error is not established numerically.
